descriptionChirho: Emotional fear or dread in response to danger, threats, enemies, or alarming situations; Arabic khafa, Korean duryeowohada, Swahili -ogopa.
Reverential awe and pious devotion toward God or a sovereign; Arabic ittaqa/khashiya/haba, Korean gyeongwehada, Swahili -cha/-mcha.
Adjectival or participial form denoting a person who reveres God, used substantively as 'God-fearer' or 'one who fears the LORD'; Arabic khaaif/muttaqi, Swahili -mcha Mungu.
Nifal participle used adjectivally to describe God, his name, deeds, or places as awe-inspiring, fearsome, or terrible; Arabic mahib/rahib/marhub, Swahili -tisha/-ogofya.
Piel intensive-causative stem meaning to frighten, intimidate, or terrify someone; Arabic akhafa/mukhif, Korean duryeopge hada, Swahili -ogopesha.
Nifal passive imperfect expressing the idea of being feared or revered, distinct from the adjectival Nifal participle; Arabic tukhsha.
Anomalous occurrence where the form is parsed as ירא but the translations indicate ראה 'to see' rather than 'to fear'; likely a Qere/Ketiv or homograph disambiguation issue.
